news.title: Weekly Roundup: Anthropic, Fireflies, and Loom
news.gist: Fireflies responded to agent traffic by publishing per-plan API limits instead of adding a fee, while Anthropic moved Claude Docs, Slides and Design onto its free tier: two bets on charging for usage rather than for access.
points: Litterst reads the Fireflies limits as generous fair use that mostly catches extreme cases such as a runaway agent, with heavier users expected to upgrade
He gives two readings of the Claude move: earn on the work done inside commodity apps, or hand occasional AI users a concrete reason to try Claude
Loom’s new Record for agents, which turns narrated screen recordings into instructions an agent can act on, is kept for the Business + AI plan
The roundup also notes Docker dropping Build Cloud minutes from its plan listings and Mistral cutting Free plan API credits

news.why: If your team reaches a tool through agents or its API, read the published per-plan limits before automating, because the cap rather than the list price may decide which tier you need.

news.title: Cursor cuts Teams 25%, from $40 to $30+ per user a month, in a slower week: 204 changes against a 221 average
news.gist: PricingSaaS’s weekly review calls 12–18 Oct a slightly slower week, led by Cursor’s Teams cut; increases ran at their usual pace, cuts ran above it, and promotions and price reveals were below normal.
points: Shopify’s higher annual Grow and Advanced prices are read as one arm of an A/B test, with monthly billing and Basic left alone
Precog swapped opaque credits for four public flat tiers, while ApprovalMax went the other way and replaced its listed prices with contact sales
PagerDuty began stating how many AI Actions each tier includes, and Buildkite and GorillaDesk now list fees that weren’t shown before
fal’s doubled Flux 3 Image edit rate is flagged as a repeat hike, and Adapt’s Managed plan cut is the week’s deepest

news.why: With cuts above their usual rate, check whether a tool you pay for, Cursor Teams especially, now lists a lower seat price than the one on your contract.

news.title: Pricing Changes: October 12–18, 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals’ digest for our week leads with Cursor selling new subscriptions only through the X Subscription, and records free allowances ending at Taskade, Gemini CLI’s personal tier and Tugboat.
points: Existing Cursor subscribers keep their old plans, and third-party models are billed at API list price from prepaid credit on Premium and above
OpenAI retired GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT and Codex on every plan, and NVIDIA removed Kimi K3 from its free NIM endpoints
Zeabur announced it is shutting down, pausing shared-cluster services in December and stopping all servers at year end
Gemini CLI still works with an API key, Vertex AI or a Code Assist licence once the personal free tier is gone

news.why: Free tiers used for prototypes or CI can vanish with little notice, so check that your tools still have a free path and what the cheapest paid plan costs.

news.title: Shopify cut Grow and Advanced plan prices back down
news.gist: Shopify raised its annual Grow and Advanced prices and dropped them back a day later, and PricingSaaS argues the flip says more about how openly companies now test prices than about Shopify’s intentions.
points: The higher prices carried no promo badge or end date, which is why the article treats them as one arm of a live experiment; Shopify hasn’t confirmed it
Customers can compare notes or screenshot prices, so a visible overnight reversal has a cost for the vendor
The advice is to stagger price tests by cohort rather than swap the whole page, and to watch whether Shopify returns to the higher prices
nums: annual Grow price per month after the reversal, down from $89
annual Advanced price per month after the reversal, down from $359
real pricing changes Pulse has logged on Shopify’s page since 1 Jan 2024
news.why: A price you see once may be a test arm, so keep a screenshot of the quote and confirm which price applies before you commit to annual billing.

stats_analysis.t: More changes cost buyers more than saved them money
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that cost buyers more vs less; the other 32 repackage
stats_analysis.p: List-price increases outnumbered cuts, 17 to 12. The rises ran from Runpod’s GPU rates and fal’s doubled image-edit price to Lindy, Motion and PeopleHR lifting entry and per-employee prices, while Dialpad’s Sales product, Adapt and Chargeflow made the deepest cuts. Most of these records come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: A third of the week involved AI
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that touch AI features or AI pricing
stats_analysis.p: AI changes ran both ways: Runpod and fal raised compute and model rates, Flux and Hostinger enlarged AI allowances, and Storylane, Wistia and Sumo Logic moved AI features onto credits. Cursor’s Teams cut, tied to the xAI bundle, is the largest AI move of the week.

stats_analysis.t: Limits tightened more often than they loosened
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that tighten vs loosen a limit
stats_analysis.p: Tighter limits hit free plans and usage caps: Sauce Labs cut parallel sessions from 24 to 5 and Voxel51 cut compute hours, both at unchanged prices. Looser ones were mostly allowance bumps, such as Expo’s build concurrency and SignWell’s free API documents. Almost all come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.figNote: changes that switch the unit a price is counted in
stats_analysis.p: Precog moved from credits to flat tiers per source, Mixmax to pricing by monthly recipients, Workleap and Pingboard added a per-manager fee, and LeadMagic now charges per returned result rather than per request. CaseMark went against the AI trend, swapping pay-per-deliverable fees for seats. Rerun your own volumes before renewal.

stats_analysis.t: The top of the list leans on price
stats_analysis.p: Six of the 11 raise prices, from Atlassian’s Bitbucket Premium to Runpod’s GPU rates, but Shopify’s rise lasted a day and looks like a test. Three are cuts, led by Cursor’s Teams seat, and Moodle’s cut simply undid its own rise from earlier in the week. Most of the 11 come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Consumers are barely touched, or we barely see them
stats_analysis.p: Business software dominates again, with 84 B2B-only changes. The consumer-only moves are small: Optery trimmed broker coverage, Strawberry Browser added a daily cap, CoinTracker cut Ultra and Colaberry made month-to-month dearer. Our feed captures for this week are also partial, covering mostly companies A to K.

news_trends.t: AI is priced by usage, not by access
news_trends.p: Poyar’s week-42 piece found variable pricing already the norm for AI-native companies, and this week Anthropic gave free users its workspace apps while handing Max subscribers API credits, betting on usage over access. Our records show the same move in packaging: Storylane, Wistia, Vizly and Sumo Logic put AI on credits.

news_trends.t: Free tiers: cut for developers, mixed elsewhere
news_trends.p: PricingSaaS counted more free-tier AI limits expanded than tightened in week 42, but this week’s developer-tool digest is all cuts: Taskade, Gemini CLI and Tugboat ended free allowances. Our records sit in between, with Snaptrude and env0 cutting free plans while Raspberry AI and GitBook gave theirs more.

news_trends.t: Price moves are a small slice of the market
news_trends.p: Two straight weekly reviews from PricingSaaS show plain increases and cuts as a small minority of all changes, with packaging, limits and promotions making up the rest. Even the headline price moves are less settled than they look: Shopify’s rise lasted one day.
